Merged the Marshall Plan's economic aid, military assistance to allies, and technical assistance into one program under one agency, with the stated purpose of strengthening the free world against Soviet power.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 65 Stat. 373](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/65/373){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Created the Mutual Security Agency to supervise all foreign aid.
- Combined military, economic, and technical assistance authorities.
- Tied aid to the recipient's contribution to collective defense.

## Why it matters

It set the Cold War pattern of treating economic and military aid as one security instrument. The [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd) was written to separate them again, which is the origin of the divide between development and security assistance. It followed the wartime model of the [Lend-Lease Act](lend-lease-1941.qmd).

## Current status

Replaced by the Mutual Security Act of 1954 and then by the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}
